result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You had a thyroid blood test (TFT) on 25 September 2026. A TFT is a blood test of the thyroid gland.
Your TSH was 7.8 mU/L. The normal range is 0.3 to 4.2. TSH is a hormone measured to check the thyroid.
The letter says your dose of levothyroxine is too low. Your dose is being increased.

## What you need to do
1. Collect your new levothyroxine prescription from your pharmacy. It is ready now.
2. Take one 25 micrograms tablet and one 50 micrograms tablet every day.
3. Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach. Take it at least 30 minutes before breakfast or other medicines.
4. Leave at least 4 hours between levothyroxine and iron or calcium tablets.
5. Do not take levothyroxine at the same time as iron or calcium tablets.
6. Have a repeat TFT blood test in 6 to 8 weeks. That is between 6 November 2026 and 20 November 2026.

## Dates and medicines
- 25 September 2026: your thyroid blood test (TFT).
- 6 November 2026 to 20 November 2026: your repeat TFT blood test is due.
- Levothyroxine: 75 micrograms once a day. The dose is increased. Your old dose was 50 micrograms.
- The new dose is one 25 micrograms tablet and one 50 micrograms tablet every day.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does levothyroxine do?
- What does my TSH result mean for me?
- Where can I have my repeat blood test?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
